observed.detail: Three-quarter pixel illustration of a compact green diesel shunter. One long low hood leads to a taller cab at the rear; nose is the grille end at image right.
Long hood has rounded shoulders and a straight, nearly level roof. Green access doors and two louvred vent panels divide the visible side; thin cream piping runs above them.

Rear cab is taller than the hood, with a grey curved roof and cream-framed blue-grey glazing. The near side shows a narrow rear pane and a larger rectangular sliding pane; the end view shows a three-pane arrangement.

Three large spoked driving wheels sit beneath the hood on the visible side. Pale steel tyre rims surround dark spokes and warm orange-brown crank pins; one straight connecting rod links all three wheels.

Nose has a tall dark radiator grille, cream upper edge trim, one round lamp above the grille, two smaller low lamps, corner grab rails, a brown buffer beam, round buffers and a central hanging coupler.
Roof fittings include three flat rectangular access covers and one short orange exhaust stack. No second stack or large fan is visible.

Opposite-end three-quarter illustration confirms the cab end has three framed windows, a small upper lamp, brown buffer beam, buffers and a central coupler. The long green hood and three-wheel side arrangement continue toward the other end.

inferred.detail: The shell and side equipment are built bilaterally, while the pictures show only one side clearly; unseen opposite-side small fittings are not claimed to match an exact prototype drawing.

Wheel axles are parallel to Y and the longitudinal body, deck edges and roof edges are parallel to X. The PNGs establish the side-view alignment; the exact real-world scale and axle spacing are not measured.
All three coupled wheels rotate at the same phase and a linked rod translates with their crank pins. The illustrations show the connection but do not specify its exact motion timing.
Internal diesel equipment, hidden frame members, exact axle bearings and the unpictured back of the nose are simplified. Standard track gauge is a rendering compatibility constraint.

omitted: Unseen cab interior, seats, dashboard and engine internals
Unpictured badges, lettering, side numbers, extra roof vents and pipes
Unverified rear-facing livery or extra rear windows beyond those in view2
Fine piping and mechanical detail too small to read in the source pictures
guidelines: Only the two hashed PNGs in this project determine appearance and shape. View1 is the workbook v9 BR Class 08 picture; view2 is the paired extracted rear reference. Build new editable primitives using the frozen C50 helpers and c50-lighter-v2 profile. Do not use any runtime geometry, fit/gear table, existing reconstruction or game screenshot as a shape source. Keep the locomotive longitudinal axis aligned to +X and parallel to the rails. Preserve visible glazing, lamps, all three coupled wheels and their moving connecting rod; use minimal inferred closures and omit unsupported detail.
